chapter: New York, Nick's and the Army
title: A patron finances his move to New York
summary: A generous woman who tips well at Blatt's Palm Gardens pays for his trip and car; he sorts out whether he left in 1940 or 1941 and finally gets Nick's.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You began to get itchy though too didn't you?
Yes - in a way. Yeah and of course, I met a very, very nice lady at that time - I shall mention

no names at this point -- but she was very interested in my career and she said to me once -- I was working at Blatt's Palm Gardens and she happened to be there-- and we played her favorite songs everytime she came in because she was a very good tipper and she once said to me, Bill, what is the most - in your mind - the most thing you would like to do-- with your career - right now -- tell me about it. And, I said --- well, there's one thing I would love to do - just love to do - is go to New York; she says - okay - you got it. And, she financed my trip to New York, bought me a car and sent me money while I was in New York and that's how I got to New York and everybody says it's '41--- I was almost certain I left there in '40; at the end of '40 ---
Well, I think I resolved that problem -- I think you went back and forth a couple of times---
Oh, I did that--- not to Milwaukee--- but to Chicago---
Yeah -- and I think this is why there's confusion in your mind and, also, in the minds of people who tried to trace you---
Well, we'll get that straightened out in the biography. But, it was in that early part - 1940-41 and '42 period, you did stop going back and forth---
